hypothesis: Reusing the fail-closed Runtime Probe containment boundary for production-replacement proof tests prevents repository-controlled Vitest code from inheriting daemon authority or reaching the host while retaining exact production-adoption verification.

metricsCompared.name: daemon authority projected into repository proof tests
metricsCompared.baseline: The direct Vitest child inherited the complete daemon process environment.
metricsCompared.candidate: The contained child receives a minimal allowlisted environment, and focused regressions reject representative daemon secret values.
metricsCompared.unit: production proof launch paths inheriting daemon authority

metricsCompared.name: repository proof isolation
metricsCompared.baseline: Vitest ran directly in the host repository with host filesystem and network access and no hard resource boundary.
metricsCompared.candidate: Proofs fail closed unless the shared Linux Bubblewrap boundary supplies offline namespaces, a disposable overlay, protected-path masking, teardown, and hard process/resource limits.

metricsCompared.name: focused security regression coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: No regression proved unavailable-sandbox rejection or prevented proof code from inheriting sensitive daemon values and writing through the host workspace.
metricsCompared.candidate: The seven-file focused suite passed 26 tests with one platform-specific skip, covering shared sandbox composition, environment filtering, fail-closed rejection, completion, task moves, and Runtime Probe containment.

rationale: This repairs a confirmed high-severity authority escape at the synchronous task-move boundary. The candidate removes the direct repository-code launcher, shares one fail-closed containment implementation with Runtime Probes, preserves production-entrypoint transform provenance and isolated assertion reruns, and has focused test, typecheck, and lint evidence. Hosts unable to establish the required OS boundary reject completion before loading repository code.
